name: Globe and Mail cryptic crossword No 3,336

clue.text: Absurd act cleaning lady handles regularly (7)

indicators.note: taking letters at regular intervals: every second one

blocks.note: a char, or charwoman, is a cleaner
the 2nd, 4th and 6th letters of hAnDlEs

annotation.surface: A cleaner makes a ridiculous show of how she handles things.
annotation.walkthrough: CHAR is an old British word for a woman paid to clean houses. A charade is a pretence so transparent it is absurd.
annotation.definitionFit: A charade is an absurd pretence, a piece of play-acting nobody believes.

clue.text: Plant bed for children on holiday (11)

blocks.note: a cot is a baby's bed
used as itself
the spring holiday

annotation.surface: A bed is set aside for the children while the family is away on holiday.
annotation.walkthrough: The clue reads as travel arrangements; only the first word is the definition. Cotoneaster is a common garden shrub with red berries.
annotation.definitionFit: Cotoneaster is a shrub, often grown for its berries and hedging.

clue.text: Touching cooking range at home singes thumb initially (7)

indicators.note: take the first letter of each word it follows

blocks.note: an Aga is a British brand of cast-iron range cooker
to be in is to be at home
first letters of Singes and Thumb

annotation.surface: Someone touches the hot range at home and burns a thumb.
annotation.walkthrough: An Aga is a big cast-iron stove found in many British country kitchens. 'Touching' is not an emotion here: a ladder leaning against a wall is touching it.
annotation.definitionFit: Something against a wall is touching it, in contact with it.

clue.text: Gold Renault newly uncovered (2,7)

indicators.note: the letters are made new, arranged afresh

blocks.note: Au is the chemical symbol for gold
the carmaker's name, rearranged

annotation.surface: A gold Renault car has just been unveiled.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Uncovered' looks like a car launch unveiling; here it means naked.
annotation.definitionFit: Au naturel is French for 'in the natural state', i.e. naked.

clue.text: Religious book’s key article absorbed by sister (6)

indicators.note: one piece is taken inside another

blocks.note: E is a musical key
Sr is the abbreviation for Sister, as in a nun's title
the definite article, placed inside S…R

annotation.surface: A sister has taken in a key article from a religious book.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Key' is a musical key here, not something that opens a lock, and 'article' is the grammar term, not a piece of writing.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the Book of Esther is one of the books of the Hebrew Bible and the Old Testament.

clue.text: Legendary beast some hermit eyed westwards (4)

indicators.note: only part of the following words is used
in an across clue, west is right to left, so read backwards

blocks.note: found in hermIT EYed

annotation.surface: A mountain hermit has been eyeing a mythical creature.
annotation.walkthrough: The hermit fits the Himalayan scene; the answer runs backwards across 'hermit eyed'.
annotation.definitionFit: The yeti is the abominable snowman of Himalayan legend.

clue.text: The old piano’s all right (3)

blocks.note: ye is an archaic spelling of 'the', as in Ye Olde Shoppe
p is the musical abbreviation for piano, softly

annotation.surface: Someone reassures us that an old piano is fine.
annotation.walkthrough: 'All right' is an informal agreement, the same as saying yes.
annotation.definitionFit: Yep is a casual yes, much like saying 'all right'.

clue.text: Recurring theme maestro penned? Not entirely (5)

indicators.note: the answer uses only part of the words before it

blocks.note: found in maesTRO PEnned

annotation.surface: A composer asks whether he really wrote the recurring theme, and admits only partly.
annotation.walkthrough: The musical surface makes 'recurring theme' sound like a leitmotif; the answer sits across the words 'maestro penned'.
annotation.definitionFit: A trope is a recurring theme or motif in art or writing.

clue.text: Coach’s temperature drops (5)

blocks.note: T is the standard abbreviation for temperature
rain is drops of water

annotation.surface: A coach's temperature is falling.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Drops' reads as a verb, the temperature falling; it is a noun, raindrops. 'Coach' is the verb too: to coach is to train.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a coach and a train are both passenger carriages on rails, and each word also has the verb sense of instructing someone.

clue.text: Quiet Aussie resident wears Scottish hat somewhere in pub (7)

indicators.note: the hat goes around the other pieces, as a hat is worn on the outside

blocks.note: a tam-o'-shanter, split around the inner pieces
p = piano, quiet in music
a kangaroo, Australia's best-known resident

annotation.surface: A quiet Australian in a Scottish bonnet sits somewhere in the pub.
annotation.walkthrough: TA(P ROO)M: the Aussie resident is an animal, not a person.
annotation.definitionFit: A taproom is a bar room in a pub or inn.

clue.text: Computer component relative stole recovered externally (11)

indicators.note: only the outside letters of the word are used

blocks.note: a mother is a relative
a boa is a long scarf or stole, often of feathers
the outer letters of RecovereD

annotation.surface: A family member's stolen computer part has been found again.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Stole' reads as the past of steal; it is the noun, a wrap worn round the shoulders.
annotation.definitionFit: The motherboard is a computer's main circuit board.

clue.text: Family member’s Asian bread (3)

blocks.note: a grandmother, in the everyday British word for her
the leavened flatbread of South Asia, also spelt with a double A

annotation.surface: A relative's recipe for flatbread.
annotation.walkthrough: In Britain 'nan' is an everyday word for grandmother.
annotation.definitionFit: Nan means both a grandmother and the South Asian flatbread.

clue.text: Longs to enter English river that’s most cool (9)

indicators.note: one piece goes inside another

blocks.note: the Trent, a major river of the English Midlands, split around the inner piece
as in 'is dying to'

annotation.surface: Someone yearns to go into the coolest English river.
annotation.walkthrough: TREN(DIES)T. 'Dying for' something is longing for it.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the slang sense: cool means fashionable, so the superlatives match, most cool standing for the most fashionable.

clue.text: Very happy with illumination during act (9)

indicators.note: one piece sits within another, as something happens within a time

blocks.note: a deed is an act, split around the inner piece
light is illumination

annotation.surface: A performer is thrilled with the lighting during their act.
annotation.walkthrough: DE(LIGHT)ED: the theatrical picture hides that 'act' is simply a deed.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: delight is great pleasure, so to be delighted is to be happy to a strong degree, which the 'very' supplies.

clue.text: Increasingly silly ignoring daughter and son for part of meal (6)

indicators.note: leave out the letter named

blocks.note: DAFTER without D, the abbreviation for daughter
s is the abbreviation for son

annotation.surface: A family gets sillier at the table, leaving out the daughter and son.
annotation.walkthrough: Daft is British for silly, so dafter is sillier. Afters is British for dessert.
annotation.definitionFit: Afters is the course that comes after the main meal: dessert.

clue.text: Location containing one fish (6)

indicators.note: the first piece holds the second inside it

blocks.note: a place is a location, split around the inner piece
the Roman numeral for one

annotation.surface: A spot where a single fish is found.
annotation.walkthrough: PLA(I)CE: the answer sounds just like the word it is built from.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the plaice, orange-spotted and flat, is one of the most common fish in British fish-and-chip shops.

clue.text: One who drinks Bier freely put under current doctor (7)

indicators.note: the letters move freely into a new order
in a down clue, the rearranged letters go below the others

blocks.note: I is the symbol for electric current
MB, Bachelor of Medicine, a doctor's degree
the German word for beer, rearranged

annotation.surface: A drinker downs German beer freely, while a doctor is on hand.
annotation.walkthrough: Bier looks like German beer, and fits a drinker; here it is just four letters to rearrange.
annotation.definitionFit: Imbibe is a formal, often jokey verb for taking in drink, especially alcohol; the agent noun names the person doing it.

clue.text: Lifted kid to pass on little flier? (6)

indicators.note: in a down clue, lifting reads the word upwards, so backwards

blocks.note: to rib someone is to tease or kid them
pass on is a euphemism for die

annotation.surface: A child is picked up and handed a small aeroplane.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Kid' looks like a child; it is the verb, to tease. The question mark flags a playful definition: a birdie is a little bird.
annotation.definitionFit: Birdie is a child's word for a little bird, which flies.

clue.text: Working the land around outskirts of Hanover is exciting (9)

indicators.note: one piece goes round the other
only the outside letters are used

blocks.note: tilling is working the soil, split after T
the outer letters of HanoveR

annotation.surface: Farming around the edges of a German city is a thrill.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Working the land' sounds like the whole farm; it is one verb, tilling, which is broken open to take the two letters.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a thrill is a sudden wave of excitement, so something thrilling is exciting in a strong, physical way.

clue.text: Rugby building that’s filthy and corroded (5)

blocks.note: RU is Rugby Union
a pigsty, a byword for filth

annotation.surface: A rugby club's building is dirty and falling apart.
annotation.walkthrough: Rugby reads as a club or a school; it is the abbreviation RU, for Rugby Union.
annotation.definitionFit: Rust is the corrosion of iron, so metal that is rusty has been corroded by air and water.

clue.text: Short straight haircut, whichever way you look at it (3)

indicators.text: whichever way you look at it
indicators.note: the answer reads the same forwards and backwards

blocks.note: the definition end: a cut level with the jaw, all one length

annotation.surface: A short straight haircut looks the same from any angle.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface teases that a bob looks the same from the front and back; really the word does.
annotation.definitionFit: A bob is a short haircut, usually straight and level with the jaw.

clue.text: Person modified Democrat’s answer (7)

indicators.note: the letters are changed into a new order

blocks.note: used as itself
D is the abbreviation for Democrat

annotation.surface: A Democrat's reply came from someone who changed their mind.
annotation.walkthrough: The 's reads as possession but works as 'has': PERSON, changed, has D to give the answer.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym with 'answer' as a verb: to respond to a question or a letter is to answer it.

clue.text: Duke penetrates Old English verse (3)

indicators.note: one piece pushes into another

blocks.note: OE is the abbreviation for Old English, split around the inner piece
D is the abbreviation for Duke

annotation.surface: A duke features in a piece of Old English poetry.
annotation.walkthrough: O(D)E: 'Old English' reads as the language of the poem.
annotation.definitionFit: An ode is a lyric poem, a piece of verse.

clue.text: Bill and Alan’s core percussive instrument (5)

indicators.note: take the middle of the word

blocks.note: a tab is a bill, as at a bar
the middle letters of aLAn

annotation.surface: Two men, Bill and Alan, share a drum at the heart of their band.
annotation.walkthrough: Bill and Alan look like two people; Bill is the tab you pay.
annotation.definitionFit: The tabla is a pair of Indian hand drums.

clue.text: Kind, extremely trustworthy and polite (4)

indicators.note: take the extremes, the first and last letters

blocks.note: the outer letters of TrustworthY
the outer letters of PolitE

annotation.surface: A description of a person who is kind, very reliable and courteous.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Kind' looks like one more nice quality in the list; it is the noun, a sort.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym with 'kind' as a noun, as in 'what kind of car': a sort or category of thing.

clue.text: Scrap with rude criminal tolerated (7)

indicators.note: the letters are treated wrongly, into a new order

blocks.note: an end is a leftover scrap, as in odds and ends
rearranged

annotation.surface: A fight with a rude criminal was put up with.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Scrap' reads as a fight; it is a leftover piece.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the past tense: to endure hardship is to put up with it for a long time, which is what tolerating means.
